first_impression.reaction: Honestly, RSVP reminders are a problem for about a year from now. I clicked because half our guests will be flying in and I wanted to know how much chasing that means. The intro gets to the point in two sentences and the second paragraph names flights, leave and per-event headcounts, which is exactly our situation, so I skimmed on. It's a solid, calm how-to with no 'dream day' nonsense. But it's a DIY guide: the work of chasing people lands on us and our parents, which is the spreadsheet life we're trying to avoid. Useful to bookmark, not what makes me enquire.

journey.quote: For a destination wedding, those replies carry more weight. Guests are arranging flights, leave and rooms, and each event across the weekend needs its own headcount.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is the bit that made me keep reading. It's written for people like us, not a local reception.

journey.section: The number of reminders to send
journey.quote: A guest who has ignored three kind notes is better reached by a call from someone they know.
journey.reaction: Sensible and human. Clear limit, no faff.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: Older relatives may prefer a call or a printed card to a link. Guests overseas need a little more thought: check their time zone before you call, and use the channel they already reply to you on.
journey.reaction: Thinking about our grandparents and the UK side of James's family. Small, practical, right.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: Split the list between families. Each partner, or each set of parents, takes their own side, so every reminder comes from a familiar voice.
journey.reaction: Good advice, but it's also a reminder that this is all on us and our parents. Mum would be delighted; I'm less sure.

journey.section: Who to remind and how to reach them
journey.quote: As general information as at November 2026, not legal advice: the Privacy Act does not cover individuals acting in a personal capacity, and in some situations state or territory laws may also apply.
journey.reaction: I'm a lawyer and even I think this is heavy for a post about nudging Aunt Carol. Accurate, but I skipped it.

journey.section: Wedding RSVP reminder text message wording
journey.quote: [Guest name]! Quick nudge from the two of us: your RSVP is the last piece of our puzzle. Reply by [reply date] at [RSVP web address] and we will save you a seat (and a glass).
journey.reaction: A bit cute. I wouldn't send 'last piece of our puzzle' to our friends, they'd screenshot it. The formal and warm versions are fine though, and at least there's a choice.

journey.section: Reminding guests for a destination wedding
journey.quote: When the celebration runs across several events, ask for a reply for each one. A guest may come to the ceremony and dinner but arrive too late for welcome drinks.
journey.reaction: This is the insider detail I didn't know I needed. Hadn't thought about per-event replies at all.

journey.section: Reminding guests for a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world, start to finish.' Every planner says end-to-end. What does that actually mean? It doesn't connect to anything in this section.

journey.section: Deciding whether to count a guest
journey.quote: Counting a quiet guest as attending is the cautious choice for catering; counting them as declined protects a tight venue capacity.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, not a fake rule. I like that it leaves the decision with us.

journey.section: Keep one list so you only remind the right guests
journey.quote: [Wonderland Studio](/wonderland-studio), our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, keeps that list in one place.
journey.reaction: Interesting, I'd look. But can James and both sets of parents use it at once? The whole article tells us to split the list between families.

journey.section: Ready to plan the weekend around the replies
journey.quote: Once the replies are in, the real planning begins: where everyone stays, how each event runs and who pays whom, and when.
journey.reaction: Hang on. For a destination wedding we'd want where everyone stays sorted long before the replies. This makes it sound like the hard part starts at the end, which isn't how it feels from where we're sitting.

journey.section: Ready to plan the weekend around the replies
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: AUD quotes and inclusions in writing go straight at my currency and hidden-cost worry. That's the most reassuring line on the page.

unanswered_questions: Can several people (us, both sets of parents) share and update the same guest list in Wonderland Studio?
Is Wonderland Studio free or part of working with an Advisor? (deferred business detail)
What does 'start to finish' include day to day for a destination weekend, and who is accountable on the day? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge for planning? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic end-to-end claim dropped into a practical section. It reads like an ad break and doesn't tell us anything we can test.

turn_offs_found.quote: [Guest name]! Quick nudge from the two of us: your RSVP is the last piece of our puzzle.
turn_offs_found.why: Slightly try-hard for our friends. Minor, because the formal and warm options sit right next to it.

would_share_with: James: the 'Reminding guests for a destination wedding' section, because per-event replies changes how we'd set up the RSVP
My mum: the 'Who to remind and how to reach them' section, since she'll be the one ringing the older relatives on her side

cta_reaction.why: No hard sell and the AUD-in-writing line is right. But we haven't picked a destination and this is a late-stage topic. I'd save the post and enquire after a destination post and a real wedding, not from here.

top_3_changes: Make the mid-page Advisor line earn its place. Replace old: 'A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone.' with new: 'A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone, which helps when the events your guests are replying to run across a whole weekend.'

Fix the closing line that makes it sound like planning starts after the replies. Replace old: 'Once the replies are in, the real planning begins: where everyone stays, how each event runs and who pays whom, and when.' with new: 'Once the replies are in, the details firm up: where everyone stays, how each event runs and who pays whom, and when.'

Tone down the light text so we'd actually send it to friends. Replace old: '[Guest name]! Quick nudge from the two of us: your RSVP is the last piece of our puzzle.' with new: '[Guest name]! Quick nudge from the two of us: we would love to know if you are in.'

VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots, meta) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the post say whether Wonderland Studio lets several family members share one guest list? The article recommends splitting the list between families, so a reader will ask.
The privacy-law paragraph in 'Who to remind and how to reach them' reads heavy for this topic. Keep as is for accuracy, or trim in a later round?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'wedding rsvp reminder' while researching how much guest management a destination wedding involves; at 14 months out with no destination, relevance is 2.
Business details (fees, Studio pricing, on-the-day accountability) are deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Fast-mode read: read the intro, takeaways, reminder timing, who to remind, destination section and close; skimmed the wording blocks and FAQ.
